With a falling VIX, a weak DXY and a positive S&P, sentiment tilts risk‑on despite ongoing wars in Iran and Yemen that add a modest bearish drag (max 2 points).

articles.title: The Pentagon Doesn’t Need to Reinvent Supply Chain Transparency
articles.snippet: As the United States seeks to rebuild its defense industrial base, Washington is scrambling to understand an industrial ecosystem that it no longer controls, nor largely understands. China has been able to achieve strategic advantage against the United States through the targeted application of export controls and licensing requirements on specific materials at specific supply chain nodes. U.S. responses, by contrast, have largely been broader in scope and shallower in effect. articles.title: PS Events: Reinventing Europe
articles.snippet: Despite boasting world-leading universities and research institutions, robust trade relationships, a strong industrial base, and a well-established rule of law, Europe has failed to leverage its advantages in a way that would unlock its full economic potential. At the same time, it appears to be punching below its weight internationally, instead of providing the leadership the world so desperately needs to maintain progress toward broadly shared goals.

articles.title: Canada's Inflation Rises to 3.1% as Fuel Oil Prices Jump 58%
articles.snippet: Gasoline and fuel oil pushed Canada's annual inflation rate to 3.1% in September, up from 3.0% in August, as the war in the Middle East kept fuel prices high, Statistics Canada said on Monday. Gasoline prices rose 27.8% from a year earlier, up from 22.8% in August, despite the switch to the cheaper winter blend. Fuel oil and other fuels rose 57.8%, up from 43.7%, with the heaviest burden in Atlantic Canada, where many homes are heated with oil. The overall energy index climbed 19%, up from 15.4%, and transportation costs rose 8.4%. Grocery prices…

articles.title: Robot Wars – How China Has the Robotics Industry in Its Grip
articles.snippet: Last year, China started requiring export licenses for rare earth magnets. Within weeks, Elon Musk was telling investors that production of Tesla's Optimus robot had been affected. That's because every humanoid robot needs up to 4.5 kilos of rare earth magnets to move, and China makes more than 90% of the world's supply. It's exactly the problem REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY) has been building to help solve. The company is putting together a rare earth supply chain outside of China, from processing in Saskatchewan to metal-making in Ohio.…
